newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's ban on MMT passes final hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Canada's ban on MMT passes final hurdle.

text.p: Canada's Senate on Wednesday passed a bill that would effectively ban the controversial gasoline additive MMT, despite threats of legal challenges.
After weeks of stalling and debate, the Liberals in the Senate pushed the bill through by limiting debate and ordering a final vote late Wednesday -- and passed on a voice vote.
It had already passed the House of Commons, Parliament's other chamber and now awaits routine royal assent.
Implementation of the bill would mean that Virginia-based Ethyl Corp, which supplies Canada with MMT, would lose its entire Canadian market unless legal challenges succeed.
The legislation would ban the import and interprovincial trade of the gasoline additive MMT or methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl.

Ethyl has threatened to launch a US$200 million legal case against the Canadian government if the bill is passed under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). And several provinces have threatened to take action to quash the law too.

MMT has been used as a replacement for lead as an octane booster. But car companies said it gummed up their on-board diagnostic systems, and some experts said MMT could be environmentally harmful and unhealthy for Canadians.

Critics of the bill said no harmful effects have been proven. They said the government was caving in to corn producers in Ontario and to auto manufacturers who were looking for a scapegoat for falling short of the government's environmental regulations.
An amendment to implement the bill only after MMT was proved to gum up diagnostic systems failed 39 to 32, a Senate clerk said.
The unelected Senate is about evenly split between Conservatives and Liberals and has been active recently in opposing bills passed by the Liberal-controlled Parliament.
